articles.title: Ukraine war briefing: Russia attacks multiple power plants after Trump energy ceasefire claim
articles.summary:
Zelenskyy says Ukrainian skies filled with Russian drones after truce claim, which Moscow has yet to confirm, as six killed in strikes. What we know on day 1,692

Russian strikes hit multiple Ukrainian power plants after Donald Trump claimed both sides had agreed to stop hitting each other’s energy infrastructure, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. The Ukrainian president said on social media a drone had hit a power plant in Kyiv on Sunday, leading to power outages in the capital. Shortly after, he said there had been a strike on the CHP-5 power plant in the eastern city of Kharkiv, adding:“Ukrainian skies have been infested with Russian ‘shaheds’ [drones] all day.”

Trump said earlier that “effective immediately, there is an energy ceasefire in the war between Russia and Ukraine”. “Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!” the US president wrote on his Truth Social platform on Sunday morning in Washington, without further details. Zelenskyy expressed surprise at the announcement, saying the deal was “news to me” and he was seeking further details. Russia has yet to confirm it agreed.

The ceasefire appeared to garner support on Sunday from Ukraine’s key western allies, including the UK, France, Canada and the European Commission. British prime minister Andy Burnham said a sustained energy ceasefire was “the best route to get energy and fuel back into world markets”. French president Emmanuel Macron said Paris supported a “real energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine.

Ukrainian officials said Russian ⁠attacks killed six people ⁠in two Ukrainian ⁠cities ​on Sunday, including a strike ⁠on a grocery store in Kharkiv, Ukraine’s second-largest city, ​where ‌three people died ‌and 20 were ‌injured. Two children were ‌among the injured, regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said. In a separate ​attack ​in western ​Ukraine, officials ​said ‌a Russian strike ​killed ​three people.

Trump’s energy truce claim came two days after he announced a controversial agreement to buy Russian diesel fuel while temporarily easing US sanctions, prompting outrage from Ukraine and its European allies, who said it would embolden Moscow. Canadian prime minister Mark Carney added to the chorus of disapproval after a Sunday call with Zelenskyy, saying the diesel deal “is in direct opposition to the efforts of Ukraine, Canada and our allies to create peace and stability in Europe”. EU chief Ursula von der Leyen also backed Zelenskyy “as he leads the fight for his people’s freedom”, while Germany foreign minister Johann Wadephul said Berlin continued to “fully support” him.

Trump lashed out at Zelenskyy when asked about criticism of the Russia diesel deal, saying it was “time for Ukraine to get a new president” who would finally settle the war. Zelenskyy pushed back, telling US ABC News on Sunday: “First of all, with all respect to President Trump, it’s up to our society, up to our people to choose one or another leader.”

The Trump administration is threatening to stop the procurement system that provides Ukraine with weapons in order to press Kyiv to halt its deep strikes on Russian energy infrastructure, the Financial Times quoted officials in Europe as saying. The US was lobbying European capitals and Kyiv in an attempt to end the attacks on Russian oil refineries, they said.

A Ukrainian ⁠drone killed one ⁠person in Russia’s ⁠border ​Belgorod region on Sunday, ⁠officials said. The operational headquarters ⁠in Belgorod ​region said the drone struck a car on a road ‌near the border. In the ​part of Ukraine’s eastern Donetsk region ⁠held by Russian ​forces, Moscow-installed ​officials ​said one ​person ‌had been killed ​in ​a Ukrainian attack.

Russia’s military ⁠said it ⁠struck ⁠a logistics ​centre in southern Ukraine’s ⁠Mykolaiv region and a cargo vessel ⁠in the ​Black ‌Sea. The logistics centre in the town ‌of Ternivka was used to ​store military and dual-use cargoes for the ⁠Ukrainian military, the ‌Russian defence ministry ‌claimed on Sunday.

Evropská centrální banka nadále upravuje své měnové směrnice v prostředí přetrvávající ekonomické nestability a globálních obchodních třenic.
archive.security_status_en: Europe is facing a wave of social unrest and protests against austerity measures and government spending (particularly in France and Belgium), while geopolitical tensions escalate due to US deals on Russian oil and ongoing attacks in Ukraine. The European Central Bank continues to adjust its monetary guidelines amid persistent economic instability and global trade friction.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí stupňujícím se bezpečnostním rizikům kvůli ruským útokům na ukrajinskou infrastrukturu a shadow válce, zatímco domácí politickou scénu zatěžují rozsáhlé protesty proti úsporným opatřením a napětí ve Francii i Bruselu. Globální trhy a vztahy s USA navíc komplikuje nečekaná americko-ruská dohoda o dodávkách nafty a sankční kroky Washingtonu vůči ICC.
archive.security_status_en: Europe faces escalating security risks from Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure and hybrid warfare, while domestic politics are strained by large-scale anti-austerity protests and student unrest in France and Brussels. Global markets and transatlantic relations are further complicated by a surprise US-Russian diesel deal and Washington's sanctions against the ICC.

Makroekonomické prostředí nadále komplikují fiskální spory v EU ohledně rozpočtových škrtů a přísnější bezpečnostní opatření včetně plánovaných vízových omezení pro ruské občany.
archive.security_status_en: Europe faces escalating security pressure due to intense Russian attacks in Ukraine and a surge in hybrid and sabotage operations across the continent. The macroeconomic environment continues to be complicated by EU fiscal disputes over budget cuts and stricter security measures including planned visa restrictions for Russian citizens.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, heightened market volatility is expected due to geopolitical tensions, security incidents, and ongoing political debates within the EU.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí stupňujícím se bezpečnostním rizikům včetně pokusu o atentát na polského premiéra Tuska a intenzivních ruských útoků na Ukrajině. Na politické scéně probíhají ostré spory ohledně návrhů EU rozpočtu, zatímco hospodářské trhy vstřebávají dopady amerických sankcí a nové dohody EU ohledně čínských elektromobilů.
archive.security_status_en: Europe faces escalating security risks including an attempted assassination plot against Polish Prime Minister Tusk and intense Russian strikes in Ukraine. The political scene sees sharp disputes over EU budget proposals, while economic markets absorb the impacts of US sanctions and a new EU agreement on Chinese electric vehicles.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, market fluctuations are expected under the influence of geopolitical news from Ukraine and ongoing European bank earnings reports.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí zvýšenému napětí v důsledku eskalace ruských útoků na ukrajinskou energetickou infrastrukturu navzdory údajnému příměří, které oznámil Donald Trump. Vnitřní stabilitu regionu navíc zatěžují domácí politické krize, sociální nepokoje ve Francii a odhalená hrozba atentátu na polského premiéra Donalda Tuska.
archive.security_status_en: Europe faces heightened tension due to escalating Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure despite a claimed ceasefire announced by Donald Trump. Regional stability is further strained by domestic political crises, social unrest in France, and a foiled assassination threat against Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, volatility in energy markets and investor caution are expected due to the escalation of the conflict in Ukraine and major bank earnings reports.
